findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, exposing credentials to anyone with instance or state access.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data at rest on the volume is unencrypted, risking data exposure if the underlying storage is compromised.
The EBS snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, so the snapshot data at rest remains unencrypted and exposed to potential unauthorized access.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to SSH brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from anywhere on the internet.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no other compensating controls (e.g., no WAF), broadening the attack surface for the web service to the entire internet.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block / bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to or tampering with sensitive network traffic logs.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to direct internet access.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to direct internet access.
